title: Alting and many: promise offered to mind and will as true and good
source_text: XVII. Denique Altingius docet proprium fidei subjectum esse partim intellectum hominis, partim voluntatem, quia promissio gratiae offertur in verbo, non modo cognoscenda & approbanda ut vera, sed etiam amplectenda ut bona; adeoque menti simul & voluntati offertur, & tam hac accipi, quam illa approbari certum est. Locor. comm. parte 1. loco 13. De Vocatione interna, & Fide justificante. Quibus consentanea tradunt Antonius Walaeus, Trelcatius, Paraeus, & complures alii, quorum testimonia sigillatim citare prolixum nimis & superfluum foret.
pass_a_gloss: Finally Alting teaches that the proper subject of faith is partly man's intellect, partly the will, because the promise of grace is offered in the Word not only to be known and approved as true but also to be embraced as good; and so it is offered to mind and will together, and it is certain that it is received by the latter as it is approved by the former (Loci communes part 1 locus 13, On Internal Calling and Justifying Faith). Antonius Walaeus, Trelcatius, Paraeus, and many others teach things agreeing with this, whose testimonies it would be too long and superfluous to cite one by one.
pass_b_english: Alting: faith's subject is partly intellect, partly will — grace-promise known as true and embraced as good.
Walaeus, Trelcatius, Paraeus, and many agree (Alting Loci 1.13).
